title: Long-Term Care Subsidies
description: Provides means-tested subsidies for long-term care services by MOH-funded long-term care providers.
highlights: For home and community long-term care services provided by MOH-funded providers: Means-tested subsidies of up to 80%
For institutional long-term care services provided by MOH-funded providers: Means-tested subsidies of up to 75%
Additional subsidies of up to 15% for Singapore Citizens born in or before 1969

sections.About this support:
**For home and community long-term care services (e.g. Day Care, Community Rehabilitation services, Home Nursing, Home Medical)**

- Means-tested subsidies of up to 80%
- Additional 15% subsidies for Singapore Citizens born in and before 1969

**For institutional long-term care services (e.g. Nursing Home)**

- Means-tested subsidies of up to 75%
- Additional 5% subsidies for Singapore Citizens born in and before 1969
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents
- Monthly per capita household income (PCHI) of less than or equal to $4,800 (or property annual value (AV) of less than or equal to $21,000 for households with no income)
- Receiving long-term care services from MOH-funded providers
sections.How to apply?: Persons who require long-term care services can approach their doctor at the hospital, polyclinic, or Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) for assistance in applying for admission to a subsidised long-term care service.
sections.Where to go: [Find nearest AIC Link](https://www.aic.sg/about-us/aic-link-locations/)

title: Healthier SG
description: A national strategy focused on preventive care to empower individuals to take steps toward better health, with the support of their Healthier SG clinic and community partners.
highlights: Receive dedicated care from your preferred Healthier SG clinic
Prevent or manage chronic conditions and complications
Create your Health Plan with your family doctor
Receive healthcare and medication subsidies and benefits

sections.About this support:
Benefits after enrolment include:

- Fully subsidised first Health Plan consultation and subsequent annual Health Plan check-ins with your enrolled Healthier SG clinic
- Healthpoints (worth $20) via Healthy 365 app after the first Health Plan consultation
- One-off Healthpoints (worth $10) via Healthy 365 app upon completing both an in-person annual Health Plan check-in and viewing of Health Plan on HealthHub within the qualifying period of 1 July 2026 to 31 December 2029.
- Special subsidies for Healthier SG screening tests and vaccinations (for eligible Singapore Citizens)
- Healthier SG Chronic Tier subsidy at Healthier SG clinics for CHAS cardholders with high medication requirements (for selected chronic medications at prices comparable to polyclinic prices)
- Full MediSave coverage for treatment of chronic conditions listed under the Chronic Disease Management Programme (CDMP), up to the relevant MediSave withdrawal limit
sections.Who is this for?: Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents aged 40 years old and above to enrol with a Healthier SG clinic or polyclinic
sections.How to apply?:
**Self-enrol via HealthHub**

If you are eligible, you will be invited via SMS to enrol in Healthier SG. You can do so in three simple steps:

1. Use the HealthHub app, which can be downloaded from Google Play or Apple App Store.
2. Choose your preferred Healthier SG clinic from the [list of more than 1,000 Healthier SG clinics](https://gowhere.gov.sg/healthiersg).
3. Book an appointment for your fully subsidised first Health Plan consultation.

For a detailed step-by-step guide on how to enrol, click [here](https://www.healthiersg.gov.sg/enrolment/guide/).

If you have not received an SMS invitation, you can:

1. Request one by submitting your details at https://go.gov.sg/healthiersg-sms-invite
2. Contact the MOH hotline at 6325 9220

**Enrol with caregiver's assistance**

You can grant your caregiver/family member/loved one access to your HealthHub, so they can use their smartphone to help you enrol in Healthier SG. Follow the step-by-step guide at these links:

- [Grant your caregiver/family member access](https://safe.menlosecurity.com/https:/www.healthiersg.gov.sg/enrolment/addcaregiver/)
- [Assist your family member’s enrolment](https://safe.menlosecurity.com/https:/www.healthiersg.gov.sg/enrolment/caregivers/)

**Other assisted enrolment**

- Visit any ServiceSG Centre or AIC Link for enrolment assistance. To find an enrolment station near you, visit [HealthierSGGoWhere](https://www.gowhere.gov.sg/healthiersg/)
sections.Where to go: To find a Healthier SG clinic or enrolment station near you, visit [HealthierSGGoWhere](https://www.gowhere.gov.sg/healthiersg/)

title: Voluntary Housing Refund
description: Allows you to return any CPF savings used for your home purchase to your CPF account while still owning your property. Doing so reduces the refund amount you would have to make and increases the cash proceeds you would get when you eventually sell or transfer your property. This also boosts your retirement savings as you can benefit from CPF interest rates.
highlights: Grow your retirement savings with CPF interest rates
Greater cash proceeds and lower required CPF refund upon property sale or transfer

sections.About this support:
- Receive more cash proceeds and refund less to your CPF account when selling or transferring your property
- Take advantage of CPF’s interest rates and retire with more
- Re-use CPF savings for the various CPF approved schemes if needed
sections.Who is this for?:
- You have used your Ordinary Account (OA) savings to purchase your property
- Please note the following conditions when making the voluntary housing refund:
  - You can refund up to the CPF principal amount withdrawn towards the property plus its accrued interest to your CPF account
  - If you are an undischarged bankrupt, you have to obtain the Official Assignee’s approval to make this housing refund
  - While housing grants will generally be refunded to your OA if you have an HDB flat, the grant(s) may be partially credited to your Special Account / Retirement Account and MediSave Account if you have received more than $30,000 in grant(s)
  - If you are 55 and above, the refunded amount [will be used to meet your Full Retirement Sum (FRS)](http://www.cpf.gov.sg/VHRAge55), which supports your retirement needs through monthly payouts
  - Any refunds beyond your cohort’s FRS will remain in your OA
- You can read more on [housing refunds and their processes](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/infohub/educational-resources/sales-proceeds-after-selling-your-home)
sections.How to apply?:
Check the amount of voluntary refund you can make under the “What happens if” section in your [Home ownership dashboard](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/homeownershipdashboard).

You can make the voluntary housing refund through the following methods:

- Log in to [my cpf digital services](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/make-a-voluntary-housing-refund) using your Singpass:
  - Choose your property and enter a refund amount

Or

- Use the CPF Mobile app:
  - Download the CPF Mobile app
  - Log in with your Singpass
  - Tap on 'Services'
  - Choose 'Voluntary Housing Refund'

[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us)

CPF hotline: [1800-227-1188](tel:1800-227-1188)

title: Home Protection Scheme (HPS)
description: Mortgage-reducing insurance that protects you and your loved ones from losing your Housing and Development Board (HDB) flat in the event of death, terminal illness, or total permanent disability.
highlights: Payout up to the sum assured will be made to HDB or the mortgagee directly
Processing of claim application generally takes 5 working days upon CPF Board's receipt of requested documents

sections.About this support:
**For claims under death grounds**

- HPS benefits will be paid in a lump sum (based on the share of HPS cover) to HDB or the mortgagee directly to settle the outstanding housing loan.
  - Any excess claim amounts will be paid to the insured member's CPF Ordinary Account.
  - Thereafter, the deceased member’s CPF savings will be distributed to nominees, or next-of-kins depending on whether there is a valid nomination made.

**For claims admitted under medical grounds**

- Housing instalments (based on the share of HPS cover) may be paid by HPS for a period of up to two years, before a review of insured member's eligibility to claim the remaining insured sum in full is carried out.
sections.Who is this for?:
CPF members who own a HDB flat and are HPS policyholders paying their monthly housing instalments using CPF savings or cash are eligible to apply for HPS coverage.

- HPS claim payout is made to:
  - Next-of-kin of HPS policyholder who is deceased, or
  - HPS policyholder who is certified by a registered medical practitioner under the Medical Registration Act to be suffering from:
    - Terminal illness: an illness that is likely to result in the death of the insured CPF member within 12 months
    - Total permanent disability: the inability to take part in any employment permanently, or the total permanent loss of physical function of any of the following:
      - Both eyes, or
      - Two limbs, or
      - One eye and one limb
sections.How to apply?:
[Apply online for HPS coverage](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/apply-adjust-home-protection-scheme-cover) via the CPF website with your Singpass.

**Claim on death grounds**

- If the insured member has an outstanding housing loan, CPF Board will automatically assess the deceased’s claim eligibility upon Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA)'s notification.
- CPF Board will inform the co-owner(s) or the insured's next-of-kin of the outcome and if additional information is required.

**Claim on medical grounds**

- Submit your application to CPF Board directly via the [CPF website](http://cpf.gov.sg/applyrleandclaimhpsdps)

title: CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS)
description: Provides CPF members an option to invest their OA and SA savings to enhance retirement funds.
highlights: Grants multiple options to invest your Ordinary Account (OA) and Special Account (SA) savings

sections.About this support: CPF members can invest their OA and SA savings in a [wide range of products](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/growing-your-savings/earning-higher-returns/investing-your-cpf-savings/cpf-investment-scheme-options) to enhance their retirement savings under the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS).
sections.Who is this for?:
- To be eligible to invest in CPFIS, you must meet all the following criteria:
  - At least 18 years old
  - Not an undischarged bankrupt
  - Have more than $20,000 in OA and / or more than $40,000 in SA
  - Completed the [CPFIS Self-Awareness Questionnaire (SAQ)](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/growing-your-savings/earning-higher-returns/investing-your-cpf-savings/cpf-investment-scheme-self-awareness-questionnaire)
- If investing in the CPFIS-OA scheme, you may only invest up to 35% of your investible savings for stocks and 10% for gold. Investible savings refers to the sum of your OA balance and the amount of CPF you have withdrawn for investment and education.
- To find out how much of your OA and SA savings can be used for investment, you may:
  - Log in to [my cpf digital services](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/ds/dashboards/investment) with your Singpass, then select “my cpf” > “My dashboards” > “Investment”
  - Log in to the [CPF Mobile app](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/cpf-mobile-app) with your Singpass, then select “Investment”
  - Visit any CPF Service Centre with your identity card
- Upon reaching age 55, you can withdraw your CPFIS-OA and CPFIS-SA investments, as well as the cash balance in your Investment Account, after setting aside the Full Retirement Sum (FRS) in your Retirement Account
  - The FRS can be set aside fully with cash / or with cash (i.e. at least the Basic Retirement Sum) and property
- Once your withdrawal application is approved, your CPFIS investments will be transferred to you. The withdrawal will not result in liquidation of your investment holdings
- Your agent bank and / or product providers will contact you about transferring your investments to you
sections.How to apply?:
- New CPFIS investors must first take the [Self-Awareness Questionnaire (SAQ)](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/growing-your-savings/earning-higher-returns/investing-your-cpf-savings/cpf-investment-scheme-self-awareness-questionnaire) before they can start investing
- The SAQ helps you to assess if you have basic financial knowledge and whether CPFIS is suitable for you
- To start investing under CPFIS-OA, open a CPF Investment Account with one of the following CPFIS agent banks:
  - Overseas-Chinese Banking Corporation Ltd (OCBC)
  - United Overseas Bank Ltd (UOB)
  - DBS Bank Ltd (DBS)
- After opening the account, approach product providers to buy or sell investments
- For CPFIS-SA:
  - Approach product providers directly to buy or sell investments

title: CPF Housing Scheme
description: Enables CPF members to use their Ordinary Account (OA) savings to buy properties and pay for various housing purchase-related costs if they are owners of the property.
highlights: Use CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings to buy properties or pay for housing purchase-related costs

sections.About this support:
- Enables members to use their OA savings to buy residential property in Singapore
- OA savings can be used to cover downpayments, housing loans, stamp and legal fees and Home Protection Scheme premiums (for HDB flats)
sections.Who is this for?:
- The amount of OA savings members can use depends on several factors, including the remaining lease of the property, the type of housing loan you’re taking, the age of the youngest owner using CPF, and the number of properties you are using CPF for
- For detailed information on the terms and conditions, please refer to the [terms and conditions for use of CPF savings under the CPF Housing Scheme](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tnc/t-c-for-use-of-cpf-under-cpf-housing-scheme)
- Upon sale, transfer or disposal of the property (during your lifetime), you are required to refund the CPF principal amount withdrawn together with the accrued interest to your CPF account(s)
- If you are aged 55 or above and have pledged the property to make up your retirement sum, you will also be required to refund the pledged amount
sections.How to apply?:
- To use your OA savings for the property, HDB or the lawyer acting for you in the purchase must submit an application to the CPF Board with your CPF withdrawal details, along with any required documentation
- [Know how much OA you can use](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/home-ownership/using-your-cpf-to-buy-a-home)
- Before your OA savings can be used, you may need to pay certain amounts in cash, [depending on the type of property and housing loan](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/can-i-use-my-cpf-savings-for-the-down-payment-of-my-property)
- Note that the savings withdrawn are paid to the property developer, HDB, sellers, banks, lawyers or such other entities on your behalf
- To adjust or stop your OA savings for your loan payments, log in to your HDB e-Services if you have an HDB loan or [myCPF](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/houseinstalment) if you have a bank loan

title: CPF Education Loan Scheme
description: A loan scheme that allows CPF member to use their Ordinary Account (OA) savings to pay for their own, children’s, spouse’s, siblings' or relatives' government subsidised tuition fees for full-time diploma/degree courses at Approved Educational Institutions (AEIs).
highlights: Allows for the use of OA savings to pay for the government subsidised tuition fees for full-time diploma/degree courses at Approved Educational Institutions (AEIs)
Applications will only be processed after the application period for the approved educational institution has closed
Processing of application generally takes 3 working days upon receipt of the student's enrolment confirmation from the approved educational institution

sections.About this support:
- Allows the use of OA savings to pay for own, children’s, spouse’s, siblings' or relatives' government subsidised tuition fees for [full-time diploma/degree courses at Approved Educational Institutions (AEIs)](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/what-courses-are-covered-by-the-cpf-education-loan-scheme)
- The student (i.e., borrower) would need to start repaying the principal amount withdrawn plus the accrued interest in cash, to the lender’s CPF OA, one year after graduating from or leaving the course of study, whichever occurs earlier

Note:

- OA savings can be used up to the Available Withdrawal Limit under the CPF Education Loan Scheme
- The Available Withdrawal Limit is either 40% of your accumulated OA savings, or your remaining OA balance, whichever is lower
- The amount that can be used is also subject to the tuition fees payable
- If you are 55 or older, you must set aside the Full Retirement Sum (FRS) in your Retirement Account before using the remaining OA savings, up to the Available Withdrawal Limit.
- You may wish to check how much tuition fees can be paid using [OA savings.](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/how-much-of-tuition-fees-can-be-paid-using-cpf-ordinary-account-oa-savings)
sections.Who is this for?:
- CPF members/lenders with OA savings are eligible to pay for their own, children’s, spouse’s, or relative’s government subsidised tuition fees using OA savings, up to the Available Withdrawal Limit
- The Available Withdrawal Limit is up to 40% of accumulated OA savings, or the remaining OA balance, whichever is lower
- The CPF member can check the Available Withdrawal Limit through the CPF website using Singpass
- Only full-time diploma / degree courses at Approved Educational Institutions (AEIs) are covered under this loan scheme
- For the list of approved courses, you may refer to [approved courses under this scheme](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/what-courses-are-covered-by-the-cpf-education-loan-scheme)
- Here are the alternative education financing options:
  - [MOE Higher Education Student Loan](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/what-is-the-moe-higher-education-student-loan-hesl)
  - [Other financing options offered by the institutions](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/what-are-the-financing-options-from-moe-and-the-educational-institutions)
  - [Post-Secondary Education Account funds](https://www.moe.gov.sg/financial-matters/psea)
sections.How to apply?:
- Apply online through [“Forms and e-applications"](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications) at [CPF website](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/apply-for-cpf-education-loan) with your Singpass
- You must read the accompanying Terms & Conditions, and Procedures & Guidelines before you complete the online form
- Before you submit your application online under the CPF Education Loan Scheme:
  - Check the application period for the approved educational institution you are applying to use CPF savings to pay your tuition fees
  - Ensure you are accepted by the institution and confirm that it is an approved educational institution under the CPF Education Loan Scheme
  - Establish whether you are a new (e.g. fresh intake for AY2024/2025) or existing student (e.g. 2nd year student) under the institution
- You are required to submit 1 (one) application form for each CPF lender, for the entire course of study, unless you enrol into a different AEI
- Please note the application period for use of CPF savings under CPF Education Loan Scheme differs for each AEI
- You may [refer to their schedules here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/apply-for-cpf-education-loan/application-schedule)

title: Large Families Scheme
description: Provides more support for Singaporean families who have three or more children.
highlights: Increased Child Development Account (CDA) First Step Grant to $10,000
Large Family MediSave Grant of $5,000
Large Family LifeSG Credits of $1,000 annually, during the years that the third and subsequent child turns 1 to 6 years old

sections.About this support:
The SG Child Support Package announced at the 2026 National Day Rally will replace the Baby Bonus Scheme and Large Families Scheme. The increased CDA First Step Grant for large families will cease from April 2027. As Child Credits will be given to all eligible children under the Package, Large Family LifeSG Credits will also cease, with no disbursements in 2027. More details on additional support for large families will be provided at a later date.

Learn more about the [SG Child Support Package](https://go.gov.sg/sgchildsupportpackage).

Families will receive additional support of up to $16,000 for each third and subsequent Singapore Citizen child, on top of existing Baby Bonus Scheme benefits.

**Child Development Account (CDA) First Step Grant**

- $10,000 CDA First Step Grant (increase from $5,000)
- For each third and subsequent Singapore Citizen child born on or after 18 February 2025
- Deposited into the eligible child's CDA within two weeks of CDA opening
- Can be used to defray approved preschool and healthcare expenses of the child and/or his/her siblings

**Large Family MediSave Grant**

- $5,000 Large Family MediSave Grant
- For each third and subsequent Singapore Citizen child born on or after 18 February 2025
- Deposited into the mother's MediSave account, following child's Baby Bonus enrolment
- Can be used to offset the mother’s pregnancy and delivery costs, or approved dependant's healthcare expenses

**Large Family LifeSG Credits**

- $1,000 annually in Large Family LifeSG Credits
- For each third and subsequent Singapore Citizen child, including those turning 1 to 6 years old in 2025
- Credits are disbursed to the CDA trustee of the child and accessible via LifeSG mobile app
- Can be used at any merchant that accepts payments using PayNow UEN QR or NETS QR, to defray household expenses
- Credits are valid for 12 months from disbursement, with the expiry date displayed in the LifeSG mobile app
sections.Who is this for?:
Families with a third or subsequent Singapore Citizen child born on or after 18 February 2025 will receive:

- the increased CDA First Step Grant of $10,000,
- a $5,000 Large Family MediSave Grant, and
- $1,000 annually in Large Family LifeSG Credits during the years that the child turns 1 to 6 years old*.

*The Large Family LifeSG Credits also applies to existing large families with at least one child aged six or below.
sections.How to apply?: No application is required.

Up to $15,000 in Government co-matching  for eligible Singaporean children

sections.About this support:
The SG Child Support Package announced at the 2026 National Day Rally will replace the current Baby Bonus Scheme and Large Families Scheme. Those currently on the Baby Bonus Scheme will be automatically transitioned to the Package. In the meantime, existing payouts will continue as usual. 

Learn more about the [SG Child Support Package](https://go.gov.sg/sgchildsupportpackage).

The Child Development Account (CDA) is a special savings account for the child, which can be used for defray child-raising costs. The First Step Grant is automatically deposited after the CDA is opened, and subsequent savings will be co-matched by the Government, up to a cap.

Eligible Singaporean children born on or after 14 Feb 2023 will qualify for the following enhanced CDA benefits announced at Budget 2023.

**Child Development Account First Step Grant:**

- $5,000 automatically credited into the CDA upon account opening.

**Government co-matching of CDA savings:**

- Eligible Singaporean children are entitled to Government co-matching up to a cap of $4,000 for the first child, $7,000 for the second child, $9,000 for the third and fourth child, and $15,000 for the fifth child and beyond.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Child is a Singapore Citizen
- Children born on or after 14 Feb 2023
- Parents are lawfully married
- Children of unwed parents may be eligible for CDA benefits if they are born on or after 1 September 2016.

title: Silver Housing Bonus (SHB)
description: Seniors aged 55 or above may receive cash bonus when they right-size to a 3-room or smaller HDB flat, and top-up the proceeds from the sale of their existing property into their CPF Retirement Account (RA) and join CPF LIFE.
highlights: Receive CPF monthly payouts for as long as they live, under CPF LIFE
Application must be submitted within 1 year from date of completion of the second housing transaction

sections.About this support:
- With effect from 1 December 2025, the SHB has been enhanced to provide greater support to seniors.
- Seniors can supplement their retirement income if they right-size from a HDB flat or private residential property with an Annual Value (AV) up to $31,000 and buy a 3-room or smaller HDB flat.
- Seniors who commit to a net increase of up to $60,000* in their CPF RA after right-sizing, with the sum going towards their retirement payouts, can qualify for an SHB amount of $30,000. They can do so using their CPF housing refunds**, if sufficient, and may no longer need to make the top-up in cash.
- They can qualify for an additional $10,000 cash bonus if they right-size to a 2-room or smaller flat, including a Community Care Apartment (CCA). This additional $10,000 bonus applies regardless of the amount they commit to their CPF RA.
- Overall, the maximum SHB amount that eligible seniors may receive is $40,000. Visit [HDB InfoWEB](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/retirement-planning/monetising-flat-for-retirement/silver-housing-bonus) for more details

* The net increase to commit in your CPF RA depends on the net sale proceeds and is capped at $60,000 per household. It is further capped by the prevailing Full Retirement Sum (FRS).

** CPF principal amount withdrawn to purchase a property and the accrued interest that needs to be refunded after selling the property.
sections.Who is this for?:
- At least 1 owner must be a Singapore Citizen (SC)
- The SC is aged 55 or above
- Monthly household income not more than $16,000
- Existing property is an HDB flat (met minimum occupation period for resale flat), or a private residential property with an Annual Value of up to $31,000
- No concurrent ownership or interest in a private residential property or in more than 1 non-residential property

Other conditions:

- Next property you are buying is a 3-room (excluding 3-room terrace) or smaller flat from HDB or from the resale market
- You must have positive net sale proceeds
- Booking of new HDB flat or application to buy resale flat must either be before sale of existing residential property, or within 12 months of completing the sale of the existing residential property
- SHB application must be submitted within 1 year from the legal completion date of the second housing transaction (either the purchase or sale)
sections.How to apply?:
- Learn about your eligibility for this scheme (and other housing monetisation options) and the estimated monthly payouts you can receive via [HDB’s 'Check Housing Monetisation Option' e-Service](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/BR05AWEnquireHMOptions)
- To apply:
  - Enquire with our Customer Relations Executive during the appointment for second housing transaction (either resale completion or new flat keys collection appointment)
  - HDB will then schedule a financial counselling session where all the details and information such as the CPF top-up amount, bonus and the monthly payout amount would be shared during the session

title: Housing Loan from HDB
description: Provides eligible buyers with financing via housing loan to purchase or take over ownership of a HDB flat.
highlights: Eligibility for up to 75% Loan-to-Value (LTV) limit for new and resale flats
Monthly instalments capped at 30% of applicants' monthly income
Concessionary interest rate for HDB housing loans

sections.About this support:
- LTV limit of up to 75% for new and resale flats
- Monthly instalments capped at 30% of the applicants' monthly income
- Concessionary interest rate for HDB housing loans
- Option to use CPF savings to pay for the loan
- Applicants may also retain their savings or use them to pay for CPF Home Protection Insurance
sections.Who is this for?:
- At least 1 applicant must be a Singapore Citizen (SC)
- The core member(s)* in the HFE letter application must not have previously taken 2 or more housing loans from HDB
- Singles aged 35 and above who are buying a 2-room Flexi flat on 99-year lease from HDB or a 5-room or smaller resale flat
- Senior citizens aged 55 and above who are not applying for a 2-room Flexi flat on a short lease or a Community Care Apartment (CCA)
- Your average gross monthly household income must not exceed:
  - $16,000 for families
  - $24,000 for extended families
  - $8,000 for singles buying under the Single Singapore Citizen (SSC) Scheme
- All persons listed in the application:
  - Cannot own or have an interest in any private residential property, local or overseas
  - Must not have disposed of any private residential property in the last 30 months before the application for an HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter

*Core member(s) refer to the applicant(s) and occupier(s) in an HFE letter application who enable the applicant(s) to qualify for a flat purchase under an eligibility scheme. All core members must remain in the flat application, and physically occupy the flat during the minimum occupation period (MOP) after the flat purchase. Their names cannot be removed.

**Second HDB housing loan**
You must also meet the following additional requirements:

At Point of Flat Purchase
Conditions to Take a Second HDB Housing Loan
You have disposed of the existing flat or private residential property and do not own any HDB flat
You and the essential occupier have to use up to 50% of the cash proceeds from the disposal of the last-owned HDB flat or from private residential property disposed of at least 30 months prior to the HFE letter application.

You may retain up to $20,000 in your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) and use the remaining balance to buy the flat.
You are buying a HDB flat **before** disposing of the existing one
You will be charged the commercial interest rate (pegged to the average non-promotional interest rate for HDB flats offered by the 3 local Financial Institutions (FIs)†) for the housing loan to buy the next flat.

The interest rate will be converted to the concessionary rate after you have disposed of the existing flat and used the CPF refund and up to 50% of the cash proceeds from the disposal to reduce the housing loan amount for the next flat. From the CPF monies refunded, you may retain up to $20,000 in your CPF OA.

†The 3 local FIs are DBS Bank Limited, Overseas-Chinese Banking Corporation Limited, and United Overseas Bank Limited.

Please note that your second HDB housing loan amount will be reduced by the full CPF refund and part of the cash proceeds from the disposal of the following residential properties:

- Existing or last-owned HDB flat
- Last-owned private residential property, disposed of at least 30 months prior to the HFE letter application

The manner of disposal includes the sale, transfer or surrender of a flat or private residential property, or by any other method under the Housing and Development Act or any other written law.

You may read more on how the cash proceeds from the disposal are used on [HDB InfoWEB](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/housing-loan/housing-loan-from-hdb).
sections.How to apply?:
- Obtain a HFE letter through the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/)
- The HFE letter will inform you of your eligibility for purchasing a flat and the amount of housing loan and grants you can receive
- Use the [payment plan calculator](https://homes.hdb.gov.sg/home/calculator/payment-plan) to estimate your budget and payments required

title: Step-Up CPF Housing Grant (Families)
description: Provides a $15,000 Step-Up CPF Housing Grant to eligible second-timer applicants buying a new or resale flat.
highlights: Eligible applicants can receive a grant of $15,000 to offset the flat’s purchase price or reduce the housing loan needed

sections.About this support:
- Supports eligible married couples and families who have taken one housing subsidy and are buying an eligible next flat.
- The $15,000 grant is directly credited into all eligible Singapore Citizen (SC) and Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) member’s CPF Ordinary Accounts. Only core applicants may use their shares to offset the flat purchase price or reduce the housing loan required.
- Eligible resale flat buyers may also apply for the Proximity Housing Grant (Families).
sections.Who is this for?:
Married couples or families who have taken one housing subsidy and meet the following conditions:

- You currently live in:
  - a 2-room Standard flat bought from HDB after October 2024, or bought on the open market with CPF housing grant(s); or
  - a 2-room unclassified flat in a non-mature estate bought from HDB after October 1995, or bought on the open market with CPF housing grant(s);
  and are buying a 3-room Standard/ unclassified flat in a non-mature estate, from HDB or on the open market.
- You currently live in a flat under the Public Rental Scheme and are buying:
  - from HDB: a 2-room Flexi or 3-room Standard flat, or a 2-room Flexi or 3-room unclassified flat in a non-mature estate; or
  - on the open market: a 2-room or 3-room Standard flat, or a 2-room or 3-room unclassified flat in a non-mature estate.

Non-mature estates include Bukit Batok, Bukit Panjang, Choa Chu Kang, Hougang, Jurong East, Jurong West, Punggol, Sembawang, Sengkang, Tengah, Woodlands, and Yishun.

- At least one core member must have worked continuously for at least 12 months during the assessment period ending 2 months before the HFE letter application, and be working at the time of application.
- Average gross monthly household income must not $8,000
- Must not own, have an interest in or dispose of any private residential property (local or overseas) in the last 30 months
- For resale flats, the remaining lease must be more than 20 years and be sufficient to cover the youngest core applicant and / or core occupier to the age of 95
sections.How to apply?:
- Apply for the HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter through the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/) to check your eligibility for this Grant and others
- If you meet the eligibility criteria, you may apply for the grant when submitting your resale application or after you have booked a flat from HDB

- You have previously received the CPF Housing Grant for Resale Flats (Singles) or bought a 2-room Flexi flat from HDB as a single, with other single citizens, or with a non-resident spouse.   - $8,000 if you bought a 2-room Flexi flat on a 99-year lease
- You and your spouse, as well as other persons listed in the application, must not have ownership or interest in any private residential property, local or overseas, and no disposal of such property within the last 30 months prior to the application

title: ComCare Assistance
description: Provides financial support for individuals and families facing varied challenges, ensuring timely aid for both short-term and long-term needs.
highlights: Cash assistance for lower-income individuals or families
[If relevant] Assistance for household and medical expenses
[If relevant] Provides other support such as employment assistance or social support services

sections.About this support:
**Interim Assistance**

Provides immediate financial assistance for lower-income individuals or families who require urgent and temporary financial relief. Assistance provided will depend on the household situation.

Interim Assistance will be enhanced and administered by MSF and the People’s Association. Applications can be made from 17 August to 31 December 2026.

**Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance**

Provides temporary financial assistance for lower-income individuals or families who are temporarily unable to work, looking for a job or earning a low income and require assistance.

- Monthly cash assistance for living expenses
- Assistance with your household bills, i.e. rental, utilities, and/or service and conservancy charges
- Medical assistance​ at public healthcare institutions
- Employment assistance such as job search and/or training
- Referrals for other relevant services

**Long-Term Assistance**

Provides long-term support to those permanently unable to work due to old age, illness or disability, and have inadequate family support or savings to rely on for daily needs.

- Monthly cash assistance for living expenses
- Assistance with medical expenses at public healthcare institutions
- Free or highly subsidised access to social support services
- LTA assistance rates according to household size:

  **Increased Rates**
  **(From April 2025)**

  $760
  2 persons
  $1,080

sections.Who is this for?:
- You must be a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident (at least one member in the same household must be a Singapore Citizen).
- Households with a monthly household income per capita of $800 and below.

**Interim Assistance**

- Greater flexibility will be exercised in assessing income eligibility.

**Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance**

- Have little or no family support, savings or assets to rely on for your daily needs.
- Looking for work or temporarily unable to work due to illness or needing to care for children, elderly or other dependants.
- Even if your income exceeds these guidelines, you can still approach a Social Service Office (SSO) for assessment if you face financial difficulties. The SSOs will assess each household’s needs, such as employment, family and finances, to ensure that the assistance we provide is holistic.

**Long-Term Assistance**

- Unable to work because of old age, illness or disability.
- Elderly persons who receive a small monthly payout from sources such as CPF Retirement Sum / CPF Life.
- Elderly persons whose children are low income themselves i.e. monthly household income per capita of $800 and below.
sections.How to apply?:
**Interim Assistance**

To apply:

- Online via [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.gov.sg/grants/smta)
- Alternatively, you may approach the following Community Partners :
  - [Social Service Offices](https://www.msf.gov.sg/our-services/directories#socialtab)
  - Community Clubs / Centres

**Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance / Long-Term Assistance**

Watch this [ComCare Financial Assistance Application Instructions video ](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fRiYpEAhIhw)which provides applicants with information on the requirements of the ComCare application process and applicants' responsibilities while on assistance.

To apply:

- Online via [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.gov.sg/grants/smta)
- Alternatively, visit your [nearest Social Service Office](https://www.msf.gov.sg/our-services/directories#socialtab) to apply in person.

Each SSO administers ComCare financial assistance and helps applicants to access other forms of assistance they may need, such as employment assistance or family services.

You'll need to provide:

- Updated bank account passbooks / account summary / bank balance enquiry slips or similar for **all members**, clearly showing the latest bank balance in the last month
- Other supporting documents, **if relevant**:
  - Your identity card or birth certificate for **all members**
(Note: NRIC/FIN of main applicants will not be required for online applications as the login will be via Singpass. If applicant / household / other family member had provided these identification documents in earlier ComCare applications, they will not be required again.)
  - Latest utility bill(s) (e.g. Singapore Power (SP), private electricity retailers)
  - Latest Medical Certificate (with duration and fitness for work status)
  - Pay-slips / Employment contract (for employment without CPF contributions)
  - Latest employment / termination letter (for recent changes in employment status)
  - Insurance Letter (for lump-sum / regular payouts by private insurer)
  - Any other supporting documents

In addition to the Personal Data Protection Act, there exists strict policies, processes and safeguards in place to ensure the proper use and protection of personal data by the Government.

- Full-time training: 50% of average income over the latest available 12-month period, with minimum allowance of $300 per month
- Part-time training: $300 per month

- SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme courses

- From 2026 Q4, long-form Workforce Skills Qualifications (WSQ) full qualifications

- Per capita monthly household income (PCHI)

title: MOE Higher Education Student Loan (HESL) Scheme
description: Loan scheme to help students who are taking MOE-subsidised diploma, undergraduate or postgraduate programmes in publicly-funded post-secondary education institutions to finance their tuition fees and borrow a living allowance loan for other education-related expenses. It also helps undergraduates to finance cost of institution-approved overseas student programme.
highlights: Base provision and means-tested balance fee coverage components under the HESL scheme can cover up to 100% of subsidised tuition fees for eligible Singapore Citizen (SC) students
Eligible students who meet the income eligibility criteria can also apply for a living allowance loan component under the HESL scheme to cover their education expenses
Loan is interest-free during the course of study; interest and repayment commence upon a student’s graduation or leaving the institution

sections.About this support:
For Diploma students
There are two loan components under HESL:
(i)     Base provision to cover up to 90% of subsidised tuition fees payable, depending on the student’s citizenship;
(ii)   Means-tested provisions
·  Loan to cover remaining 10% of subsidised tuition fees (for SC only)
·  Living allowance loan of up to $3,200 per academic year
For Undergraduate and Postgraduate students
There are two loan components under HESL:
(i)     Base provision to cover up to 90% of subsidised tuition fees payable, depending on the student’s citizenship;
(ii)   Means-tested provisions
· Loan to cover remaining 10% of subsidised tuition fees (for SC undergraduates only)
· Living allowance loan of up to $4,100 per academic year (for full-time undergraduate students only)
· Loan to cover up to $12,000 for the cost of one institution-approved overseas student programme (for full-time SC undergraduates only)
sections.Who is this for?:
The HESL will be available to the following students, and the loan components available will depend on the student’s citizenship and level of study:

- SC, Singapore Permanent Resident (PR) and international student (IS) studying full-time MOE-subsidised diploma courses in any of the local polytechnics.
- SC and PR studying full-time MOE-subsidised diploma courses in Institute of Technical Education (ITE).
- SC and PR studying full-time MOE-subsidised diploma and undergraduate programmes in LASALLE College of the Arts (LASALLE), Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts (NAFA) and University of the Arts Singapore (UAS).
- SC, PR and IS studying full-time MOE-subsidised undergraduate, full-time MOE-subsidised postgraduate by coursework, and full-time/part-time MOE-subsidised postgraduate by research programmes in autonomous universities.
- SC studying part-time MOE-subsidised undergraduate programmes in autonomous universities.

Depending on the level of study and type of institution, the means-tested loan provisions are for:

- SC and PR with gross monthly household per capita income (PCI)^ of $3,500 or less.
- IS with gross monthly household PCI of $1,875 or less.

^Monthly PCI is computed based on total monthly gross household income (GHI) divided by number of family members living in the same household.
sections.How to apply?:
- The following students can apply for HESL via the new [StudentLoanSG (SLSG)](https://go.gov.sg/slsg) portal from July 2026.
  - Newly matriculated students in Academic Year (AY) 2026 intake; and
  - Existing students (before AY2026 intake) who do not have Tuition Fee Loan (TFL) and Study Loan (SL) for their current course of study.
- Refer to the respective institution website for details on application window period and application procedures.
- Existing students who have already taken up TFL and/or SL will continue to receive their current loan provision.  No action is required from them.  However, if they wish to apply for new or additional loan provision under the HESL scheme, they should first approach their institution for advice and assessment of needs.

sections.Who is this for?:
- Child is a Singapore Citizen or a Permanent Resident (at least one immediate family member in the same household must be a Singapore Citizen)
- Both you and your spouse are each working at least 56 hours a month
- Child must attend a Student Care Centre registered with MSF
- For children attending SCCs aged 7 to 14 years old (Primary 1 to Secondary 2) in the calendar year in which subsidies commence, the monthly gross household income must be $4,500 or less for families with 4 or fewer members, or monthly household income per capita must be $1,125 or less for families with 5 or more members.   For children attending SSCCs aged 7 to 18 years old in the calendar year in which subsidies commence, the monthly gross household income must be $9,200 or less for families with 4 or fewer members, or monthly household income per capita must be $2,300 or less for families with 5 more members. Please visit [Enabling Guide by SG Enable](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/child-adult-care/special-student-care-centres) for more information on the subsidies.

**How Income is Calculated**

- For salaried employees:
Based on average gross monthly income over 12 months from CPF records or the latest IRAS assessment (within the last 2 years).
Includes: basic salary, bonuses, commissions, overtime pay, allowances, cash rewards, and employee CPF contributions.
- For self-employed individuals:
Based on average trade income over 12 months from the latest IRAS assessment (within the last 2 years), or income declared to CPF Board.

**Note:** Family members refer to the child’s grandparents or siblings below 21 years old who live at the same address, are not working or have no income, and are Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.

Your gross monthly income will be determined via HOMES as part of the means-test.

For further information, please refer to [MSF | Student Care Fee Assistance](https://www.msf.gov.sg/what-we-do/student-care/for-parents/student-care-fee-assistance).
sections.How to apply?:
All SCFA applications must be submitted online via [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/scfa)  at least six months before the intended start date. For example, if you wish to apply for SCFA effective from January 2027, you may submit the application from July 2026 onwards. SCFA approval will commence from the month in which the application is received, or from the month following the expiry of any existing SCFA, whichever is later.

[Click here to learn more about the SCFA application process.](https://www.msf.gov.sg/docs/default-source/student-care/scfa-infographic---application-process.pdf)

- If you're unemployed or looking for work, you will need to provide supporting documents (for example, proof of job search, medical letter, or medical certificate).
- With the SCFA, if you still face difficulties with the monthly co-payment of your child's student care fees, you may submit an appeal through the SCC, along with supporting documents detailing the change in circumstances and an explanation of the reasons for the appeal. Appeals will be considered on a case-by-case basis, and if approved, will commence from the month when the appeal was submitted

Monthly allowance ranging from S$1,800 to S$2,400, co-funded by the government and host organisations

sections.About this support: Jointly introduced by the Ministry of Manpower (MOM), Skills & Workforce Development Agency (SWDA), GRIT provides fresh graduates with meaningful traineeships in both private companies and public agencies, enhancing their employability and work readiness.
sections.Who is this for?:
All trainees must fulfil the following criteria:

- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident; and
- Graduated or graduating in 2024, 2025 or 2026 from Universities, Polytechnics, Institute of Technical Education (ITE) and other Educational Institutions (e.g. private universities and overseas institutions); or
- Graduated earlier from above institutions and completed National Service in 2024, 2025 or 2026.** **
- Applicants must have no prior working experience and must be prepared to commit to a full-time traineeship.
sections.How to apply?: Traineeship opportunities will be progressively made available on [MyCareersFuture.](https://www.mycareersfuture.gov.sg/)
sections.Phone number:
Hotline: [6669 7932](tel:66697932)
 Monday - Friday: 8:30am to 5:30pm
 Saturday, Sunday & Public Holidays Closed

title: Mid-Career Pathways Programme (MCPP)
description: A full-time attachment programme for mature, mid-career individuals seeking a career switch. Applicants are attached to a host organisation for 4-6 months to gain industry-relevant skills and experience.
highlights: Full-time attachment programme of 4 to 6 months with training allowance with approved host organisations
Trainees can look forward to a full-time role with their host organisations if their performance is assessed to be satisfactory during the attachment
Apply through the MyCareersFuture portal

sections.About this support:
- Offers full-time attachment opportunities of between 4 to 6 months to support mature mid-career jobseekers in widening their professional networks and gaining meaningful industry-relevant skills and experience

**Training Allowance**

Mature mid-career trainees will receive a training allowance of up to $3,800 per month for the duration of the attachment or programme. The approved monthly training allowance may vary depending on the scope of the attachment proposed by the host organisation. The government co-funds the training allowance with the host organisation.

Monthly Training Allowance
$1,800 to $3,800
Government Funding
70% of the training allowance
sections.Who is this for?: - All Singaporeans and Permanent Residents aged 40 and above
sections.How to apply?: Apply for attachment opportunities through [MyCareersFuture](https://mycareersfuture.gov.sg).

title: SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme
description: Provides temporary financial support of up to $6,000 over 6 months to involuntarily unemployed individuals, to support them in finding a job that makes better use of their skills and experiences.
highlights: Payouts of up to $6,000 over 6 months
To qualify for payouts, individuals will have to apply online to participate in the scheme and take part in supported job search activities

sections.About this support:
- Payouts of up to $6,000 over 6 months
- To qualify for payouts, individuals will have to apply online to participate in the scheme and take part in supported job search activities
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, aged 21 and above
- Earned an average gross monthly income of $5,000 or less in the past 12 months*** **(excluding employer CPF contributions)
- Previously employed in Singapore for at least six months in the past 12 months
- Unemployed due to involuntary reasons such as retrenchment, cessation of business, dismissals or termination due to illness, injury or accident
- Lives in a property in Singapore with annual value of $31,000 or less
- Has not received a payout from this scheme in the past three years

*** **Average gross monthly income includes basic salary and extra wages such as overtime pay, commissions and bonuses. This includes only the period(s) where the individual is employed and earning an income.
sections.How to apply?: You can learn more and apply for the scheme at https://go.gov.sg/jobseekersupport

title: Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS)
description: Enables parents to set aside CPF savings for the long-term care of children with special needs.
highlights: Parents may nominate child to receive payouts from their CPF savings after they pass on
Minimum monthly payout is $250, parents may decide on a higher amount
Submit the application and supporting documents to SNTC via email or mail

sections.About this support:
- Parents may nominate child with special needs to receive payouts from their CPF savings after death with minimum monthly payout of $250.
- If the nominating parent’s CPF savings upon his/her demise is insufficient to support a year’s worth of payout (e.g. a minimum monthly payout is S$250 x 12 months = S$3,000), the CPF savings will be disbursed as a lump sum to the nominee with special needs.
sections.Who is this for?:
The nominating applicant should be:

- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- The parent or an appointed legal guardian of the child with special needs

The child with special needs should:

- Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:
  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment
  - A visual impairment: Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye
  - A hearing impairment: Moderate hearing loss or worse in the better ear
  - Intellectual disability
  - Autism

Proof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional.

**Or**

- is attending or had attended a Special Education School

The 6 ADLs are:

- Eating
- Bathing
- Dressing
- Transferring
- Toileting
- Walking or moving around
sections.How to apply?:
Before proceeding, all applicants are encouraged to check if your child’s disability status has already been verified.

Find out more here: https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification

You can apply by submitting the completed [application form](https://www.sgenable.sg/snss) and supporting documents:

- via mail to Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS), Future Care Planning Resource Centre by SG Enable, 22 Lengkok Bahru, Vista, Enabling Village #03-03  Singapore 159824
- via email to [futurecareplanning@sgenable.sg](mailto:futurecareplanning@sgenable.sg).

You'll need to provide copies of:

- Nominating applicant's and child's NRIC
- Child's Birth Certificate

If your child's disability status has not been verified:

- Supporting document from the SPED school issued on the school’s official letterhead stating that the Person with Special Needs (PSN) is currently attending or has previously attended the SPED school or
- [Disability Verification Form (DVF) ](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)completed by a Registered Healthcare Professional*

After mailing the application and upon approval by MSF, parents will receive an eligibility letter, which they should bring to the CPF Board to make the SNSS nomination.

*Please note that a submitted Disability Verification Form (DVF) does not mean that your child’s disability status has been verified.

title: Special Needs Trust
description:
Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC) is a not-for-profit trust company and a registered charity. As a fully owned subsidiary of SG Enable, SNTC provides affordable trust services to safeguard monies set aside by caregivers to fund the long-term care needs of their beneficiaries who are persons with disability. 

The Special Needs Trust (SNT) is a legal arrangement for SNTC to hold monies for persons with disability (PWD).
highlights: Sponsorship schemes eg GOAL+ are available to enable lower-income families set up the Special Needs Trust with $5,000.

sections.About this support:
After the Special Needs Trust (SNT) is set up, SNTC works with caregivers to put in place proper plans and arrangements that will enhance the financial well-being of PWDs (Beneficiary).

The SNT pathway is as per the following:

1. Caregiver opens an SNT account with an initial deposit of 5,000
2. Beneficiary receives gifts under the caregiver’s will, CPF cash and insurance nominations

Disburse funds to the beneficiary upon the caregiver’s passing or incapacity according to latter’s wishes set out in the Letter of Intent.

1. The trust fund is managed by the Public Trustee and principal value is guaranteed by the Government. SNTC fees are 90-100% subsidised by the Ministry of Social and Family Development.
2. Reviews are conducted periodically to check on the beneficiary's well-being.
3. Case Managers will advise caregiver on the future care needs of the beneficiary through a personalised care plan.
sections.Who is this for?:
Caregivers (Settlor) setting up the SNT should be:

- 21 years and above
- Has mental capacity
- Not an undischarged bankrupt

Persons with Disability (Beneficiary) must be:

- A Singaporean or Permanent Resident
- Residing in Singapore
- Has a verified disability
sections.How to apply?: To start the Special Needs Trust journey, please contact SG Enable for an appointment with a Case Manager at [futurecareplanning@sgenable.sg](mailto:futurecareplanning@sgenable.sg).

title: Home Caregiving Grant (HCG)
description: Provides financial support to help with caregiving expenses for households caring for persons with moderate to severe disabilities.
highlights: Payouts of $200, $400 or $600 per month
Processing time takes up to 4 weeks
Apply through AIC’s eService portal (eFASS)

sections.About this support: Monthly cash payout of $200, $400 or $600
sections.Who is this for?:
Care recipient must meet the following criteria:

- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident with a parent, child or spouse who is a Singapore Citizen
- Lives in Singapore
- Always requires some assistance on a permanent basis with at least 3 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living (ADLs)
- Monthly per capita household income of less than or equal to $4,800 or less  (or property annual value of $21,000 or below for households with no income)
- Those with multiple properties will receive the lowest HCG payout of $200 per month
- [Not in a residential long-term care institution](https://www.aic.sg/financial-assistance/home-caregiving-grant#q5a)

The 6 ADLs are:

- Eating
- Bathing
- Dressing
- Transferring
- Toileting
- Walking or moving around
sections.How to apply?:
You can apply:

- Online at the [AIC eService Portal](https://efinance.aic.sg/)
- At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us)

You'll need to provide:

- [Completed Functional Assessment Report](https://edge.sitecorecloud.io/agencyforinb6cc-agencyforin73f5-production08ac-d178/media/agency-for-integrated-care/Files/Financial-Assistance/Functional-Assessment-Report.pdf) from your General Practitioner, a registered Nurse or a registered Physio/Occupational Therapist
- NRIC details
- Bank details
sections.Where to go: [Contact Us | AIC](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)

title: CPF Housing Grant for Executive Condominiums (ECs)
description: Provides up to $30,000 subsidy for eligible first-timer applicants buying an Executive Condominium (EC).
highlights: CPF Housing Grant of up to $30,000 for eligible first-timer household
Grant can be used to offset EC purchase price or reduce required housing loan

sections.About this support:
- Housing subsidy of up to $30,000 for eligible first-timer recipients purchasing an EC from a property developer
  - The Grant can be used to offset the EC’s purchase price or reduce the required housing loan for it
sections.Who is this for?:
- Your core family nucleus must include at least 1 first-timer applicant who has not received any housing subsidies before
- Applicants must be Singapore Citizens at least 21 years old
- The household must include at least 1 other Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- All applicants and occupiers must have no ownership or interest in private property locally or overseas in the last 30 months
- All persons listed in the application can, as a household, own up to 1 non-residential property
- Grant amount eligibility will be [determined by your household’s average monthly household income (includes all applicants and occupiers listed in the EC application)](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/executive-condominiums/cpf-housing-grant)
- All members of the core family nucleus will receive equal shares of the grant, fully credited into their CPF Ordinary Accounts
- Only core applicants can use their grants to pay for the EC unit purchase
sections.How to apply?: Contact the property developer directly for details on the application process and required documents.

title: Housing Loan from Financial Institutions (FI)
description: Supports your flat purchase through housing loans from Financial Institutions (FI) regulated by the Monetary Authority of Singapore.
highlights: Loan-to-Value (LTV) limit up to 75% of the flat’s purchase price / resale price and value
Repayment period up to 30 years

sections.About this support:
- LTV limit of up to 75% for both new and resale flats
- Repayment period of up to 30 years
- Option to use any amount in OA for flat purchase, dependent on [certain applicable limits](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/housing-loan/housing-loan-from-financial-institutions)
- Can refinance the housing loan with another loan from a different FI or a different interest rate package
sections.Who is this for?:
- Applicants must pay at least 5% of the flat price or flat value (whichever is lower) in cash. The minimum cash payment is dependent on applicants’ age, loan period and whether there are any outstanding housing loans
- Applicants who want to purchase a unit from a property developer under the Executive Condominium Housing Scheme must take a housing loan from an FI
- LTV limit is up to 75% of the flat purchase price or flat value, whichever is lower. FIs may have restrictions on flat purchase depending on remaining lease of the flat and / or if your repayment period exceeds 25 years or you have additional housing loan(s)
sections.How to apply?:
- [Compare housing loan packages from participating Fis](https://homes.hdb.gov.sg/home/calculator/budget)
- Apply early for an In-Principle Approval (IPA) from participating FIs through HDB’s Integrated Loan Application service on the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp28/TimeLine/my-flat-dashboard) for an indicative assessment of your loan eligibility
- You need to obtain a valid Letter of Offer (LO) to confirm the loan offer from an FI before signing Agreement for Lease for a new flat or exercising the Option to Purchase for a resale flat
- Use the integrated loan application service on the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp28/TimeLine/my-flat-dashboard) to apply for IPA and LO)

title: Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (Singles)
description: Provides up to $60,000 in Enhanced CPF Housing Grants (EHG) (Singles) for eligible first-timer applicants buying a new or resale flat on their own, or with their non-resident spouses.
highlights: EHG (Singles) Grant of up to $60,000 for eligible first-timer applicants
Additional up to $60,000 grant for joint singles scheme (a total of up to $120,000)
Households with lower household incomes will receive a larger grant amount

sections.About this support:
- The EHG (Singles) Grant provides up to $60,000 to offset the purchase price of the flat / reduce the required housing loan for the flat (new or resale)
- Receive a total Grant of up to $120,000 when jointly purchasing flats with other eligible first-timer single applicants (Limited to 2, up to $60,000 each)
sections.Who is this for?:
- First-timer applicants aged 35 or above, who are:
  - buying a HDB flat alone or with other first-timer single citizens
  - buying a resale flat alone, with other first-timer single citizens or with their parents
- First-timer applicants aged 21 or above who are buying a resale flat with their non-resident spouse
- If you are buying a flat with your parents, you and at least 1 parent must be a Singapore Citizen, and both parents must be first-timers and meet all the eligibility conditions
- Applicants have worked continuously for at least 12 months, 2 months before the HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter application, and were employed at the time of the HFE letter application
- Monthly household income not exceeding $4,500 for singles and $9,000 for joint singles, non-resident spouses or your parents (resale flats only)
- Flat has a remaining lease of more than 20 years
- To qualify for the full EHG grant, flat must have sufficient lease for the coverage of the youngest core applicant and occupier to the age of 95
- Must not own, have an interest in or have disposed of any private residential property (local or overseas) within the last 30 months
- All persons listed in the HFE letter application can, as a household, own up to 1 non-residential property at HFE letter application and up to 30 months before HFE letter application
sections.How to apply?:
- Obtain an HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter through the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/) to determine your eligibility for this Grant as well as others
- If you meet the eligibility criteria, you may apply for the grant when submitting your resale application or after you have booked a flat from HDB
- The Grant will be credited to the CPF Ordinary Accounts of eligible household members
- Only core applicants can use their share of the housing grants to pay for the flat purchase

title: Staggered Downpayment Scheme
description: Eases home purchase by allowing eligible first-timer couples and right-sizing flat owners to pay downpayment in 2 parts.
highlights: Ease home purchase by splitting flat downpayment into two parts
Can pay in cash and / or CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings

sections.About this support:
- Downpayment split into 2 instalments for easier financial management
- First instalment is paid at the signing of the Agreement for Lease and is either 5% or 10% of the purchase price (depending on your choice of housing loan)
- Second instalment is paid at key collection and is either 20% or 35% of the purchase price (depending on your choice of housing loan and the Loan-To-Value (LTV) limit)
- Can be paid in cash and / or CPF OA savings (including CPF housing grant, if eligible), depending on loan type
- For flat applications received from young couples eligible for deferred income assessment from the Jun 2024 sales exercise:
  - First instalment is capped at 2.5% of the purchase price
  - Second instalment is either 22.5% or 42.5% of the purchase price (depending on your choice of housing loan and the LTV limit)
  - Applicants who acquire a housing loan with a 75% or 55% LTV limit from a Financial Institution will have to pay at least 5% or 10% of the purchase price or value (whichever is lower) in cash before disbursement
sections.Who is this for?:
- First-timer couples, including those with 1 second-timer applicant
- Valid HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter obtained on or before the younger applicant's 30th birthday
- Booked an uncompleted 5-room or smaller flat in any HDB sales exercise
- Flat owners right-sizing to a 3-room or smaller flat in non-mature estates who have not completed the sale of their existing flat at the time of HFE letter application and booked an uncompleted 3-room or smaller flat in a non-mature estate in any HDB sales exercise
sections.How to apply?: Buyers will be informed during the flat booking appointment if they are eligible.

title: Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (Families)
description: Provides up to $120,000 for eligible first-time applicants applying as a family to assist with new or resale flat purchases.
highlights: Up to $120,000 Enhanced CPF Housing Grant for first-timer families
The Grant can be used to offset the flat purchase price or reduce the required housing loan
Households with lower household incomes will receive larger grants

sections.About this support:
- Up to $120,000 for applicants purchasing a new or resale flat as a family
- Up to $60,000 for couples comprising a first-time and second-time applicant
- The grant amount is based on the average gross monthly household income, with lower-income households receiving more support
- The Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (EHG) can be used to:
  - Offset the purchase price of the flat
  - Reduce the housing loan required for the flat purchase
sections.Who is this for?:
- Applicants forming a core family nucleus, consisting of the core applicant(s) and occupier(s)
- Average gross monthly household income of $9,000 or below for first-timer households (including all applicants and occupiers)
- For mixed households (first-timer and second-timer), half of the average gross monthly household income must not exceed $4,500
- If you are buying a flat with your parents, you and at least 1 parent must be a Singapore Citizen, and both parents must be first-timers and meet all the eligibility conditions
- Have worked continuously for at least 12 months, 2 months before the HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter application, and were employed at the time of the HFE letter application
- Flat has a remaining lease of more than 20 years
- To qualify for the full grant, flat must have sufficient remaining lease to cover the youngest core applicant and/or core occupier to the age of 95
- Must not own, have an interest in or disposed of any private residential property (local or overseas) within the last 30 months
- All persons listed in the HFE application can, as a household, own up to 1 non-residential property at HFE letter application and up to 30 months before HFE letter application
sections.How to apply?:
- Obtain a HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter through the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/) to determine your eligibility for this Grant and others
- If you meet the eligibility criteria, you may apply for the grant when submitting your resale application or after you have booked a flat from HDB
- The Grant will be credited to the CPF Ordinary Accounts of eligible household members
- Only core applicants can use their share of the housing grants to pay for the flat purchase

title: Fresh Start Housing Scheme
description: Helps families with children who are currently living in public rental flats to own a 2-room Flexi flat or 3-room flat on a shorter lease.
highlights: Enhanced CPF Housing Grant of up to $120,000 for eligible first-timer families
Fresh Start Housing Grant of $75,000 for eligible second-timer families
Resale levy cap of $30,000 for eligible second-timer families
HDB Concessionary Loan is subject to credit assessment

sections.About this support:
**Both first-timer and second-timer families**

- Purchase a 2-room Flexi or 3-room Standard flat on a shorter lease in HDB sales launches i.e. Build-To-Order (BTO) or Sale of Balance Flats (SBF) exercises, or open booking of flats
- HDB Concessionary Loan is subject to credit assessment

**First-timer families**

- Enhanced CPF Housing Grant of up to $120,000

**Second-timer families**

- Fresh Start Housing Grant of $75,000 ($60,000 will be disbursed into CPF Ordinary Accounts before key collection; $15,000 may be disbursed after key collection into CPF Ordinary Accounts over 5 years)
- Resale levy cap of $30,000
sections.Who is this for?:
- Have at least 1 parent and 1 child who are Singapore Citizens
- Applicant and spouse (if applicable) must be aged at least 35 and below 55 years old
- Child must be aged below 21
- Household monthly income of $7,000 and below
- Stayed in public rental flat for at least 1 year
- Have occupied public rental flat for at least 1 year, without accumulating 3 or more months of rental arrears in the preceding 12 months
- Have not received any public rental tenancy discount under Relocation, Sale of Flat to Sitting Tenants, or Rent & Purchase Schemes
- Do not own other properties overseas or locally, and have not disposed of any within the last 30 months
sections.How to apply?: You can apply online at the [HDB website](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/AA11AWFreshStartAppWeb/AA11PFreshStartNote).

title: Proximity Housing Grant (Singles)
description: Provides up to $15,000 for eligible singles buying a resale flat to live with, or near, their parents or children.
highlights: Proximity Housing Grant (PHG) of $15,000 for singles living with parents or child
PHG of $10,000 for singles living near parents or child (within 4km)
If applicant is living near them, parents / child may be residing in either a HDB flat or private residential property to meet the PHG criteria

sections.About this support:
- Receive a PHG of $15,000 if living with parents or child
- Receive a PHG of $10,000 if living within 4km of parents or child
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen aged 35 or above, buying alone, with other single citizens or with their parents
- Singapore Citizen aged 21 or above, buying with a non-resident spouse
- The parents/child helping to qualify for the PHG must be Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident
- Applicants buying a resale flat to live with, or within 4km of, their parents or child
- If parents/child are living with you, they must be included in the resale flat as co-applicants or essential occupiers
- If your parents/child are living in a private residential property they do not own, it must be owner-occupied by immediate family members i.e. child, adopted child, parent(s) or parent(s)-in-law, or siblings
- The resale flat has a remaining lease of more than 20 years
- Applicants must not have received the PHG before
sections.How to apply?:
- Obtain a HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter through the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/)
- If you meet the eligibility criteria, you may apply for the grant when submitting your resale application

title: Housing Subsidy - Citizen Top-Up
description: Provides a $10,000 housing subsidy for eligible Singapore Citizen/ Permanent Resident households when a family member becomes a Singapore Citizen.
highlights: $10,000 housing subsidy for eligible Singapore Citizen/ Permanent Resident households when a household member acquires Singapore citizenship
Citizen Top-Up  is credited into CPF Ordinary Accounts of eligible family members
Can be used for repayment or redemption of housing loan, future HDB flat purchase or CPF withdrawal at age 55

sections.About this support:
- $10,000 housing subsidy for eligible households when a qualifying member becomes a Singapore Citizen
- The subsidy is converted into equal shares and credited fully into the CPF Ordinary Accounts of eligible family members
- Only core flat owners can use their share of the CPF housing grants to pay for the flat e.g. loan repayment
- The Citizen Top-Up can be used for a lump sum repayment or full redemption of an HDB housing loan
- For housing loans from financial institutions, you may additionally use it for monthly instalments
  - You must clear all outstanding housing loan arrears before you can use the grant for the above purposes
- If you have any remaining Citizen Top-Up balance and no housing loan, you may use it to buy another HDB flat in the future, or to form part of the CPF funds available for withdrawal under CPF rules at age 55
sections.Who is this for?:
- Households that have paid a $10,000 premium when buying a flat from HDB
- Households who received a reduced Family Grant for a resale flat, a Design Build and Sell Scheme flat or an Executive Condominium unit
- The Citizen Top-Up is granted when a Permanent Resident spouse, parent, child or sibling^ originally listed in the flat application obtains Singapore Citizenship, or when a Singapore Citizen child is born to the Singapore Citizen applicant and spouse originally listed in the flat application

^ For siblings, this qualification only applies to flats purchased as orphaned siblings or for families with a non-resident spouse.
sections.How to apply?:
Submit your application online:

- Use the [Application for Citizen Top-up e-Service](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg//webapp/AB22AWTopUpGrantWeb/AB22PMain#) within 6 months of meeting the citizenship criteria

title: Enhancement for Active Seniors (EASE)
description: Subsidy for Singapore Citizen households with at least one senior who meets age criterion and needs help to install senior-friendly fittings.
highlights: Up to 95% subsidy of improvement costs
Respond within 14 working days upon receipt of application
Apply via EASE e-Service or Mobile@HDB

sections.About this support:
- Depending on your flat type, the subsidy can cover up to 95% of the total improvement cost.
- ['Calculate Calculate Cost of HIP/ EASE Improvement Items' e-Service](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/DJ02AWFNCALV7/Main)
  - Choose ‘EASE (Direct Application)’ under the selection type, indicate your flat type and the EASE improvements you wish to have.
- If you are a senior living in a rental flat, your preferred EASE improvement items will be fully funded by the Government.
sections.Who is this for?:
Singapore Citizen household with a senior who is aged:

- 65 and above; or
- Between 60 and 64, and requires assistance for one or more of the Activities of Daily Living (ADLs):
  - Eating
  - Bathing
  - Dressing
  - Transferring
  - Toileting
  - Walking or moving around
sections.How to apply?:
You can apply:

- [Apply for Enhancement for Active Seniors (EASE) Online via EASE](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/BN37AWEASE/BN37PMain.jsp)
- Mobile@HDB

You are required to submit a [Functional Assessment Report](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/-/media/managing-my-home/upgrading-and-redevelopment/enhancement-for-active-seniors-ease/FAR-Sep-2025.pdf) if you are a Singapore Citizen flat owner with at least one member in the household aged between 60 and 64 who requires assistance for one or more of the Activities of Daily Living (ADL)

- The Functional Assessment Report for the elderly aged between 60 and 64 must be endorsed by a qualified assessor such as a Singapore Medical Council fully registered doctor, and must be submitted together with your application form
sections.Where to go: [Book an appointment via e-Appointment service](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/BF13AWAppointmentWeb/branch/)

title: CareShield Life / ElderShield Supplements
description: Provides additional benefits, like higher payouts, for CareShield Life or ElderShield policyholders.
highlights: Supplement premiums can be paid using cash or MediSave for flexibility in payment
Can acquire multiple supplement policies to suit your needs
Grants extra coverage in addition to your existing CareShield Life or ElderShield plan

sections.About this support:
- Complements your CareShield Life or ElderShield plan with enhanced coverage, providing extra benefits such as increased monthly payouts
- Flexibility to buy multiple supplement policies for enhanced coverage
- Premiums for Supplements can be paid thru cash or by using your or your family member’s MediSave, limited to $600 per calendar year per insured person
