description: Provides subsidies to seniors for mobility and assistive devices or home healthcare items.

sections.About this support:
To support ageing in place, you may apply for the following subsidies for seniors who live at home:

- Subsidies of up to 90% for approved mobility and assistive devices (e.g. mobility aids such as walking/quad stick, wheelchair, geriatric chair, commodes, pressure relief mattress/cushions, hospital beds, spectacles, hearing aids, etc.)
- Subsidies of up to 80% for approved home healthcare items (e.g. milk feeds, diapers, etc.)
sections.Who is this for?:
- 60 years old and above
- Singapore Citizen or PR
- Monthly household income per capita of less than or equal to $4,800 (or property annual value of $21,000 or below for households with no income)
- Pass a [means-test](https://aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Seniors-Mobility-and-Enabling-Fund---Mobility-and-Assistive-Devices#faq) for Intermediate and Long-Term Care (ILTC) services
- Seniors and persons with disabilities will be served under one scheme and agency throughout their lifetime
- If the individual has tapped on Assistive Technology Fund (ATF)^ before the age of 60, they will continue to be served by ATF throughout their lifetime and not SMF
- If the individual has not tapped on ATF subsidies before the age of 60, they would be served by SMF throughout their lifetime
- Individuals can approach their care provider, e.g. hospitals, community care organisations, social service agencies, to enquire about their eligibility for the schemes
- They may also approach the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) if they are not currently receiving support from any care provider

^ATF provides subsidies for persons with disabilities (PWDs) to purchase the assistive technology devices to enable independent living

Additional criteria for assistive devices:

- Assessed by a qualified assessor to require the device
- Must not reside in a nursing home or sheltered home

Additional criteria for motorised devices:

- Must not have a full-time caregiver or domestic worker
- Unable to use a manual wheelchair independently
- Assessed to be mentally and physically able to safely use the motorised device

Additional criteria for home healthcare items:

- Must not be a current recipient of subsidies for the same items
- Must be receiving Home Nursing, Home Medical, Home Palliative Care, or Day Hospice services
sections.How to apply?:
You can apply:

- via the therapist or social worker at the hospital, day rehabilitation centre, or senior care centre from which your loved one is receiving care
- online [using Singpass](https://for.sg/smf-application-using-singpass) or [without Singpass](https://for.sg/smf-application-not-using-singpass)
- By mailing the [completed application form for assistive device or mobility device](http://edge.sitecorecloud.io/agencyforinb6cc-agencyforin73f5-production08ac-d178/media/agency-for-integrated-care/Files/Financial-Assistance/SMF-Application-Form.pdf) and supporting documents to Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund (SMF), No. 7 Maxwell Road #04-01, MND Complex Annex B, Singapore 069111

You'll need to provide:

- Copy of Applicant's NRIC (front and back) or a copy of the digital NRIC available on SingPass
- For first time application for motorised device, doctor memo or [Need for Assessment form](https://edge.sitecorecloud.io/agencyforinb6cc-agencyforin73f5-production08ac-d178/media/agency-for-integrated-care/Files/Financial-Assistance/Cerification-of-Medical-Need-Form.pdf) indicating need for motorised device must be submitted.

CPF transfer to
Remarks
Yourself
You can transfer your Ordinary Account (OA) savings to your SA if you are below 55.

How much you can transfer depends on your age and CPF balances.
Loved ones 
(parents, parents-in-law, grandparents, grandparents-in-law, spouse and siblings)

The amount of CPF transfers you can make to them depends on how much your loved one can receive, and the amount you can transfer.

- For more information on your [eligibility for cash transfers, CPF top-ups etc., please refer here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/growing-your-savings/saving-more-with-cpf/top-up-to-enjoy-higher-retirement-payouts)

sections.About this support:

title: CPF LIFE
description: CPF Lifelong Income For the Elderly (CPF LIFE) is a national longevity insurance annuity scheme that provides you with monthly payouts no matter how long you live.
highlights: Monthly payouts for life
Offers various plans to suit individual preferences and needs
Option to start payouts at a later age up to age 70, where monthly payouts will increase by up to 7% for each year of deferral

sections.About this support:
- Provides a lifelong monthly payout to protect against outliving one’s savings
- Unlike private annuity plans, which are subject to investment market returns, CPF LIFE monies are guaranteed by the government and earn a risk-free interest of up to 6% per annum
- Offers various plans to suit individual preferences and needs:

Escalating Plan
Increasing monthly payouts to help you maintain your lifestyle when prices increase.
Standard Plan
Steady monthly payouts even if you may have to keep within a fixed budget and adjust your lifestyle when prices increase.
Basic Plan
Payouts that will get progressively lower when balances fall below $60,000. You may have to lower your lifestyle further when prices increase.

- Option to start payouts at a later age to receive up to a 7% increase in monthly payout.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident born in 1958 and after, with at least $60,000 in the Retirement Account when you start your monthly payouts, will be automatically included in CPF LIFE
- If you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident who is not automatically included in CPF LIFE, you can still choose to join CPF LIFE as long as you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, anytime from 65 to one month before you reach 80
- You can choose to be exempted from CPF LIFE if you have a pension or private annuity plan that pays the same or higher monthly payouts than as CPF LIFE
sections.How to apply?:
- CPF Board will send you a notification three months before your 65th birthday on the options you have about your CPF savings and how you can make an informed decision using the Plan my monthly payouts service
- If you have not instructed the CPF Board regarding your payouts by then, your payouts will automatically start when you turn 70 under the LIFE Standard Plan

  - Annual Value of Residence not more than $21,000
  - Owns not more than 1 property

- You can check your eligibility via your [Retirement Dashboard](http://cpf.gov.sg/retirementdashboard)

RA savings refers to the RA balances (excluding amounts such as interest earned), plus retirement withdrawals and CPF LIFE premium deducted. If you are below 55 or turning 55 in the assessment year and your RA has not been created at the time we assess your eligibility, your total Special Account and Ordinary Account savings will be used for the eligibility assessment instead.

^^ Current Basic Retirement Sum for 2026.

Apply through a therapist or social worker at public hospitals or social service agencies

sections.About this support:
- Subsidy of up to 90% of the cost of the required assistive technology device (lifetime cap of $40,000)
- Subsidy amount is determined according to the applicant's monthly household income
- Funds can be used to buy, replace, upgrade, or repair assistive technology devices
- The Fund does not support consumables. The Fund will cover medical devices (e.g. oxygen concentrators and suction pumps) and spectacles for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents at or above age 60, who remain served by ATF.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents
- Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:
  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment
  - A visual impairment: Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye
  - A hearing impairment: Moderate hearing loss or worse in the better ear
  - Intellectual disability
  - Autism

Proof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional.

Undergone qualified assessor’s assessment to determine the need and type of device(s)

- Monthly Per Capita Household Income of $4,800 and below
- Annual Value (AV) of residence reflected on NRIC of $21,000 and below for households with no income

**Note for Singaporean and Permanent Resident Seniors:**

Subject to eligibility,

(a) Singaporean and Permanent Resident seniors who have not tapped on ATF before the age of 60 will be supported by the Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund (SMF). Please apply to SMF.

(b) Singaporean and Permanent Resident seniors who have tapped on ATF before the age of 60 will be supported by ATF throughout their lifetime.

Additional Outpatient Care Subsidies
- Additional subsidies for outpatient care at polyclinics, public Specialist Outpatient Clinics and Community Health Assist Scheme clinics.
Special MediShield Life Premium Subsidies
- Supports Pioneers in paying their MediShield Life premiums with special premium subsidies of up to 60%.

- Grants life-long cash assistance of $100 each month for those needing permanent assistance with at least 3 out of 6 of the following Activities of Daily Living:

  - Bathing
  - Dressing
  - Transferring
  - Toileting
  - Walking or moving around
[Incentives have ceased]
CareShield Life Additional Participation Incentives

description: Supports eligible individuals in their tax payments through various payment arrangements such as longer GIRO-based instalment plans.

sections.About this support:
- Longer instalment plans may be made available for individuals or businesses facing financial challenges or other extenuating circumstances
- Eligible retirees may apply for the Extended Giro Scheme for Residential Property (Retirees), which provides a longer instalment plan of up to 24 months for property tax payment
sections.Who is this for?:
For individuals who experience unexpected or extenuating circumstances due to the following:

- Financial issues
- High medical expenses
- Loss of employment or income
- Lawsuits
  - You may be required to submit documentary evidence to support your request for a longer instalment plan

For retirees:

- To be eligible for the Extended Giro Scheme for Residential Property (Retirees), applicants must meet all the following conditions:
  - You are residing in the property (and taxed at owner-occupier tax rates)
  - Your assessable income for Year of Assessment 2023 does not exceed $34,000
  - All property owners, including yourself, are aged 65 or above in 2024
  - There is outstanding property tax payable for the property

If applicants cease to be eligible, their extended instalment plan will be reverted to the standard instalment plan
sections.How to apply?:
For individuals:
- Apply for an extended instalment plan via the 'Apply for Payment Plan' digital service through the IRAS [myTax Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg)

title: Supplementary Retirement Scheme (SRS)
description: Provides tax relief to encourage individuals to save for retirement, over and above their CPF savings. Investment returns are tax-free before withdrawal and only 50% of withdrawals are taxable at retirement.
highlights: 50% tax concession on withdrawals from SRS at retirement
Tax relief on SRS contributions

sections.About this support:
- Provides equivalent tax relief on contributions to SRS, capped at $15,300 for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents and $35,700 for foreigners
- Investment returns on SRS contributions are tax-free before withdrawal, and only 50% of withdrawals will be taxable at retirement
sections.Who is this for?:
- You can only have 1 SRS account at any point in time
- To open an SRS account, you must:
  - be at least 18 years old.
  - not be an undischarged bankrupt.
  - have the mental capacity to make own decisions
  - not have an existing SRS account (including suspended accounts) with the same or another operator
  - not have a pending application with another SRS operator.
  - not have a previous SRS account with all its funds withdrawn, on medical grounds or after reaching the prevailing retirement age (at time of your first contribution)
- To qualify for SRS Tax Relief:
  - You must be a tax resident for the Year of Assessment following the year of SRS contribution
  - Your SRS account was not suspended on 31 Dec of the year of contribution
  - You did not withdraw, from your SRS account, the same amount as you contributed in the same year of contribution
- Please note that the following conditions / criteria apply to SRS withdrawals:
  - SRS withdrawals can be made anytime. Withdrawals can be made in cash or in the form of investments
  - Withdrawals are subject to income tax (based on the time and circumstances of withdrawal) and will be considered part of your taxable income
  - Foreigners and Permanent Residents who make withdrawals are subject to withholding tax
  - Withdrawals made before retirement age will be subject to penalties unless they were made due to exceptional circumstances.

You may read up on the additional criteria and details on [SRS withdrawals and the relevant taxes here](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/special-tax-schemes/tax-on-srs-withdrawals).
sections.How to apply?:
- To open an SRS account:
  - Choose 1 of 3 SRS operators (DBS Group Holdings Ltd, Overseas-Chinese Banking Corporation (OCBC) Ltd, United Overseas Bank (UOB) Ltd.) to set up an SRS account with
  - Tax relief will be provided automatically, if eligible
- For foreigners:
  - You must complete the [SRS Declaration Form](https://www.iras.gov.sg/media/docs/default-source/uploadedfiles/doc/annual-declaration-form-for-supplementary-retirement-scheme.doc?sfvrsn=e34e4cdd_22)

Note: You must update your SRS bank operator if you become a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, even if you have already contributed this year, as your maximum contribution amount will have to be recalculated and may be pro-rated.

description: Provides tax relief to eligible operationally ready National Servicemen (NSmen) to recognise their contributions to National Service, as well as to the wives and parents of NSmen to recognise the support they give to their husbands or sons.

- NSman Wife Relief of $750 for the wives of eligible NSmen
- NSman Parent Relief of $750 for each parent of the eligible NSman
sections.Who is this for?:
**NSman Self Relief:**

- Completed full-time National Service under the Enlistment Act or deemed to have completed such service by the proper authority
- Not a regular in the following organisations:
  - MINDEF
  - Singapore Police Force
  - Singapore Civil Defence Force
  - Central Narcotics Bureau
  - Singapore Prison Service
- Have not committed disciplinary or criminal offences in the preceding work year
- If you and your son are both NSmen, you will be eligible for either the NSman Self Relief or NSman Parent Relief, whichever is higher

**NSman Wife Relief:**

- You are a Singapore Citizen in the previous year
- Your husband is eligible for Nsman Self Relief
- Widows of deceased NSmen may also be eligible unless they have re-married

**NSman Parent Relief:**

- You are a Singapore Citizen in the previous year
- Your child is eligible for NSman Self Relief
- Your child was born to you and your spouse or ex-spouse / is your step-child / was legally adopted
- Parents of deceased NSmen are also eligible
- If you and your son are both NSmen, you will be eligible for either the NSman Self Relief or NSman Parent Relief, whichever is higher

title: Stamp Duty Remissions for Transfer of HDB Flats within Family
description: Provides stamp duty remission for eligible transfers of HDB flats within families.
highlights: Remission on BSD and SSD for HDB flat transfers among immediate family

sections.About this support: Remission of Buyer's Stamp Duty (BSD) and Seller's Stamp Duty (SSD) on transfer of HDB flat between immediate family members.
sections.Who is this for?:
- The incoming lessee must be immediate family of any remaining lessee of the flat and a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Repayment goes to the outgoing lessee's Central Provident Fund (CPF) account
- At least 1 of the flat’s current lessee remain after the transfer. Also, they must have either:
  - acquired the flat and paid stamp duty on its initial acquisition
  - acquired the flat via mutual exchange and paid stamp duty then
  - acquired the flat by assent, distribution or being pursuant to a will
  - acquired the flat via the right of survivorship as a joint tenant
sections.How to apply?:
- Visit the [e-Stamping Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/estamping/) to e-Stamp and obtain the remission certificate
- In order to e-Stamp, you must prepare written confirmation from HDB that confirms that the incoming lessee will form a family nucleus with the remaining lessee and is authorised by HDB to stay in the flat
- If there is no incoming lessee, HDB confirmation is not required
sections.Where to go: [Visit your nearest branch](https://www.iras.gov.sg/contact-us/locate-us)

title: Stamp Duty Remissions for Married and Divorced Couples
description: Provides various stamp duty remissions for eligible couples buying new residential property or transferring their current one(s) as part of matrimonial proceedings.
highlights: Full Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) remission for couple’s joint purchase of first residential property
ABSD remission for a couple’s jointly purchased second property
Receive Buyer’s Stamp Duty (BSD), ABSD and Seller’s Stamp Duty (SSD) remissions when transferring property due to matrimonial proceedings

sections.About this support:
- For married couples:
  - Full ABSD remission for married couple’s joint purchase of their first residential property
  - Partial ABSD remission for married couple’s joint purchase of a second residential property
- For couples undergoing matrimonial proceedings:
  - Potential remission of BSD, ABSD and SSD on property transfers resulting from matrimonial proceedings
sections.Who is this for?:
Please refer to the following table for the various conditions and scenarios where a couple may receive remissions:

Joint purchase of first residential property by married couple
While ABSD will be applicable upon stamping, you may apply for the ABSD remission instead if you meet these conditions:
- Married couple with at least 1 Singapore Citizen spouse
- Property must be jointly purchased under couple’s names only
- Both spouses do not already own any residential properties at the time of purchase
Joint purchase of second residential property by married couple
- ABSD has already been paid on the second property
- Married couple with at least 1 Singapore Citizen spouse
- Property must be jointly purchased under couple’s names only
- Couple must not own or have an interest in more than 1 residential property each when purchasing second property
- Couple’s first property must be sold within 6 months after either:
  - Date of purchase of the second property (for completed property)
  - Issue date of the Temporary Occupation Permit (TOP) / Certificate of Statutory Completion (CSC), whichever is earlier, if the property was uncompleted at the time of purchase
Couples undergoing matrimonial proceedings
- Transfer of property is due to either:
  - Court-ordered division of matrimonial assets (e.g. a proceeding for a decree of divorce, judicial separation or nullity of marriage under the law or religion)
  - Result of divorce proceedings
- Property must be transferred from 1 party to another (both involved in the matrimonial proceedings)
- Property may also be transferred by any child or children of the marriage / former marriage of the parties
sections.How to apply?:
- For partial ABSD remission for married couple’s joint purchase of a second residential property:
  - Navigate [e-Stamping Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/estamping/) to "Request" > "Apply for Refund"
  - For “Sale & Purchase – Purchase/ Acquisition” forms submitted on or after 2 Jul 2023, ABSD will be automatically refunded to the purchasers, within 6 weeks from the stamping of the first property’s sale, without needing a refund application
  - For stampings before 2 Jul 2023, you must manually provide the Stamp Duties (Spouses) (Remission of ABSD) refund application via the [e-Stamping Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/estamping/) > "Request" > "Apply for Refund"
- For full ABSD remission for married couple’s joint purchase of their first residential property:
  - e-Stamp via the [e-Stamping Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/estamping/) to obtain the remission certificate
  - Alternatively, a legal representative, where engaged, will assist with the stamping

For Remission of ABSD for a Married Couple: [View more details](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/stamp-duty/for-property/appeals-refunds-reliefs-and-remissions/common-stamp-duty-remissions-and-reliefs-for-property/remission-of-absd-for-a-married-couple)

title: Qualifying Child Relief (QCR)/Child Relief (Disability)
description: Provides tax relief to parents to recognise their efforts in supporting their children.
highlights: Claim up to $7,500 per dependant
Can be applied alongside the Working Mother’s Child Relief (WMCR) scheme for additional support
Parents may share the QCR / Child Relief (Disability)

sections.About this support:
- QCR of $4,000 per qualifying child
- Child Relief (Disability) of $7,500 per child with disabilities
- Eligible working mothers can also apply for Working Mother's Child Relief (WMCR) in conjunction with the QCR / Child Relief (Disability) for additional support
- Parents may share the QCR / Child Relief (Disability) based on an agreed apportionment
sections.Who is this for?:
**To be eligible for QCR, you must meet all the following conditions:**

During the previous year,

- Your child is unmarried and is either:
  - Born to you and your spouse / ex-spouse
  - A stepchild
  - Legally adopted
- Your child was either:
  - Below 16 years old
  - Above 16 years old and studying full-time at any university, college or other educational institution
- Your child did not have an annual income exceeding $8,000.

**To be eligible for Child Relief (Disability):**

- Your child must be unmarried / have been unmarried in the previous year and is either:
  - Born to you and your spouse / ex-spouse
  - A stepchild
  - Legally adopted
- Your child meets any of the following criteria:
  - Your child is certified by a doctor to require assistance in any of the 6 Activities of Daily Living:
    - Washing or Bathing
    - Dressing
    - Feeding
    - Toileting
    - Transferring
    - Mobility
  - Your child is certified by a doctor to be impaired in any of these 3 areas:
    - Self-Care and Activities of Daily Living
    - Compliance to Psychiatric Treatment
    - Education or Work
  - Your child is attending (or is recommended by a doctor to attend) a Special Education (SPED) school
  - Your child is not attending a SPED school but has significant special educational needs, resulting in severe functional impairments

** **

**Conditions related to claiming WMCR together with QCR / Child Relief (Disability):**

- The total claimable relief for QCR, Child Relief (Disability) and WMCR combined is capped at $50,000 per child
- When claiming both QCR / Child Relief (Disability) and WMCR, the QCR and Child Relief (Disability) claims will take precedence. WMCR claims will only be applied after.
sections.How to apply?:
**Please refer to the following processes to apply for QCR:**

**For e-Filing**

- If claiming QCR for the first time, log in to [myTax Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/login/selection) using your Singpass or [Singpass Foreign user Account (SFA)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/digital-services/others/singpass-foreign-user-account-(sfa)-for-foreign-individuals)
- Navigate to "Individuals" > "File Income Tax Return"
- Select "File" to File Income Tax Return
- Go to "4. Deductions, Tax Reliefs and Rebates"
- Select “Add New” > “Child".
- Fill in the relevant information and select “Update”.
- If you were previously approved for relief last year, the amount will be pre-filled and granted to you automatically this year
- If you would like to make changes, please follow the above e-Filing process for first-time applicants

**For paper filing**

- Complete the "Child Relief" section in Form B1 & B
- Include your child's details in Appendix 2 if it's your first time claiming

**Please refer to the following processes to apply for Child Relief (Disability):**

For first-time Child Relief (Disability) claims, email 1 of the following documents via [myTax Mail](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/login/selection)

- Completed Tax Relief Form - [Application for Claim of Disability Related Tax Reliefs](https://www.iras.gov.sg/media/docs/default-source/uploadedfiles/application-for-claim-of-disability-related-tax-reliefs.doc?sfvrsn=442cf660_28)
- Letter / supporting documents from the disability association / SPED school in respect of your child, providing details of their disabilities, to IRAS

If your child is attending / has been recommended to attend a SPED school or has significant special education needs, please refer to the [“First-time Child Relief (Disability) claims” section on the Qualifying Child Relief (QCR)/Child Relief (Disability) page)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs/qualifying-child-relief-(qcr)-handicapped-child-relief-(hcr)) for more details.

title: Merdeka Generation Package
description: Supporting Merdeka Generation seniors in their silver years by helping them to stay active, healthy and providing peace of mind over future healthcare costs.
highlights: Provides various health-related benefits to support seniors’ ageing, such as additional Outpatient Care subsidies and additional MediShield (MSHL) premium subsidies

sections.About this support:
Provides the following benefits to support healthcare for Merdeka seniors:

Additional Outpatient Care Subsidies
Additional subsidies for outpatient care at polyclinics, public Specialist Outpatient Clinics and Community Health Assist Scheme clinics.
Additional MediShield Life Premium Subsidies
Provides an additional 5% subsidy for your annual premiums, increasing to 10% after turning 75 years old.
[Redemption has ended wef. 31 Dec 2023] 
$100 Passion Silver Card Top-Up
One-off $100 top-up for use on active ageing programmes, public transport, merchant benefits etc (redemption has ceased wef. 31 Dec 2023).
[Top-Up has ended] 
Annual MediSave top-ups of $200 (2019-2023)
$200 Medisave top-ups annually from 2019 to 2023. 

MediSave can be used to cover hospitalisation and treatment costs, pay various medical-related premiums etc.
[Incentives have ceased]
CareShield Life Additional Participation Incentives
Provides participation incentives (totalling $3,000 spread across 10 years) for seniors who join CareShield Life by 31 Dec 2024, in addition to any other premium subsidies seniors may receive.

If you would like [more details on the above benefits as well as other useful information about this Package, please refer here](https://go.gov.sg/mgpackage).
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizens who were:
  - born from 1 January 1950 to 31 December 1959; and became citizens on or before 31 December 1996, or
  - born on or before 31 December 1949; became citizens on or before 31 December 1996; and are not currently receiving the Pioneer Generation Package
- You may check your eligibility via the LifeSG app or the [Singpass Mobile app](https://app.singpass.gov.sg/)
sections.How to apply?:
- No application required
- Eligible individuals will receive the benefits automatically

For general enquiries on Merdeka Generation eligibility, MediSave top-ups and MediShield Life Subsidy: [1800-222-2888](tel:1800-222-2888)

title: MediShield Life Premium Subsidies
description: To keep MediShield Life premiums affordable, the Government provides several premium support measures, such as Premium Subsidies, Pioneer Generation Subsidies and Merdeka Generation Subsidies.
highlights: Premium subsidies of up to 60%
Pioneer and Merdeka Generation subsidies

sections.About this support:
**Eligibility criteria for Premium Subsidies:**

- Premium Subsidies of up to 60% for eligible lower-to middle-income households
- Pioneer Generation Subsidies of between 40-60%, depending on age
- Merdeka Generation Subsidies of between 5%-10%, depending on age

As of 1 Apr 2025,

Household Monthly Income Per Person
Subsidy Range (tiered by age)
$0 - $1,500
25% - 60%
> $1,501 - $2,600
20% - 55%
> $2,601 - $3,600
15% - 40%

Note: The above subsidy rates apply to those living in property with an AV of $21,000 or less. Properties with an AV between $21,001 and $31,000 receive 10% less subsidies. Permanent Residents (PRs) receive half the subsidy rate applicable to Singapore Citizens (SCs). Those who live in residences with an AV above $31,000 or own multiple properties will not receive these subsidies.

**Eligibility for Pioneer Generation Subsidies:**

- Applicable for Pioneers, regardless of their household monthly income or the AV of their residence

**Eligibility for Merdeka Generation Subsidies:**

- Applicable for Merdeka Generation seniors, regardless of their household monthly income or the AV of their residence, on top of the Premium Subsidies that the seniors may be eligible for

Please [click here](https://www.moh.gov.sg/healthcare-schemes-subsidies/medishield-life/medishield-life-premiums-and-subsidies) for more information on Premium Subsidies, Pioneer Generation Subsidies and Merdeka Generation Subsidies.
sections.Who is this for?:
Eligibility criteria for Premium Subsidies:

- Household monthly income per person of $3,600 or below; and
- Living in property with an Annual Value (AV) of $31,000 and below; and
- Not owning more than 1 property
sections.How to apply?: The subsidies that you are eligible for will be automatically applied to your MediShield Life premiums.

title: MediSave Maternity Package
description: Enables applicants to claim up to $3,670 for pre-delivery medical expenses and baby delivery expenses from MediSave.
highlights: Covers both pre-delivery and delivery expenses as well as hospital charges
Medisave claims of up to $900 and $2,770 for pre-delivery and delivery expenses (depending on procedure)

sections.About this support:
- Claim up to $900 for pre-delivery medical expenses including pre-natal consultations, ultrasound scans, medications and tests
- An additional surgical withdrawal limit ranging from $1,120 to $2,770 depending on the type of delivery procedure
- Claim $1,130 per day for the first 2 days of hospital admission and $400 from the third day onwards
sections.Who is this for?:
- Applicants must have a MediSave account
- Services must be provided by public or private healthcare institutions in Singapore
sections.How to apply?:
- Submit pre-delivery medical bills to the hospital where the baby was delivered and inform the hospital that you would like to use your MediSave to pay for your expenses
- The hospital will submit the MediSave claims to CPF Board on your behalf for both pre-delivery and delivery expenses
- The claimable Medisave amount is capped by the total bill or withdrawal limit, whichever is lower

description: Provides financial support for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents who are unable to afford their MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums (where applicable) even after Government subsidies and MediSave use and have limited family support.
highlights: Financial aid for those who cannot afford premiums after subsidies and with insufficient MediSave, and have limited family support
Covers MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums (where applicable) for the next 2 policy years, as well as any outstanding premiums
Open to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents living overseas

sections.About this support: Covers MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums (where applicable) for the next 2 policy years upon approval.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Eligibility for APS is based on:
  - The financial means of the applicant and his/her immediate family members
- You will not be eligible for APS if you have sufficient MediSave to pay for your MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums or have purchased an Integrated Shield Plan and/or ElderShield/CareShield Life Supplements
- If you are granted APS and purchase an Integrated Shield Plan and/or ElderShield/CareShield Life Supplement afterwards, you will stop receiving APS
sections.How to apply?:
- You will be invited to apply for APS if you have insufficient MediSave and have limited family support to help you pay for your MediShield Life premiums
- The invitation will include an application form with details on the application process, which must be submitted along with the relevant supporting documents
- There is no need for you to apply for APS ahead of time
- Applications may take up to 20 working days to be assessed, and applicants will receive a notification on the application outcome

title: ABSD Concession for Single Singapore Citizen Seniors
description: Provides single Singapore Citizen seniors (aged 55 and above) a refund for the Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) on their second residential property purchase.
highlights: Refunds ABSD for eligible seniors who have purchased their second property

sections.About this support: Fully refunds the ABSD for eligible seniors on their second residential property purchase.
sections.Who is this for?:
Eligibility for the ABSD refund is subject to the following conditions:

- You must be a single Singapore Citizen senior (aged 55 and above) who purchased a second residential property on or after 16 February 2024
- You have paid the ABSD on the second property
- Your first residential property is solely owned by you (single Singapore Citizen aged 55 and above) / co-owned by you and your immediate family members^ (all are single Singapore Citizens aged 55 and above)
- The owners of the first residential property must also be owners of the second
- Any additional owners purchasing the second residential property with the owners of each first residential property must also be single Singapore Citizens aged 55 and above who are immediate family members
- The buyer(s) can only own up to 1 residential property each when purchasing the second property
- All buyers must not have purchased or acquired any other residential property since the purchase of the second residential property
- The first residential property must be sold or disposed of within 6 months of either:
  - the date of purchase of the second property (for completed property)
  - the date of issue of the Temporary Occupation Permit / Certificate of Statutory Completion whichever is earlier (for incomplete property)
- No change in ownership of the second property at the time of the first property's sale
- The value^^ of the second property must be less than each of the first properties that were sold
- The application for ABSD refund must be made within 6 months after the date of sale of the first property

^ Immediate family members refer to one's parent, child, or sibling.

^^ The “value” refers to the higher of the property’s purchase price or market value. The second property’s value is calculated as at its date of purchase. The first property is as at its date of sale.
sections.How to apply?:
- Apply for the ABSD refund online through the [e-Stamping Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/estamping/) with these steps:
  - Select "Request" then "Apply for Assessment / Appeal"
  - Select "Assessment (including remission and penalty)"
  - If the document is stamped, select "Yes" and enter the Document Ref No., then click “Continue” to fill in the rest of the details and submit the form
  - If the document has not been stamped, please stamp it and pay the ABSD before applying for the ABSD Concession
  - To stamp the document, select “Stamping” > “Sale & Purchase – Purchase/Acquisition” then select the relevant form (e.g. For purchase of residential property, select the “Sale and Purchase Agreement” or “Acceptance to Option to Purchase” document description and fill in the details)
- At the “Supporting Documents” page, under “Additional Information”, please key in “ABSD Concession for Single SC Seniors”
- Please also submit both the following supporting documents with your application:
  - Copy of the exercised Option to Purchase / Sale and Purchase Agreement (if applicable) for the purchase of the second residential property
  - Copy of the exercised Option to Purchase / Sale and Purchase Agreement (if applicable) for the sale of the first residential properties
- For successful applicants, the refund will be made to the party liable for payment of stamp duty.
